title: Readable status summary and tenant replay paths
body:
Purpose:
This doc contains a short status update suitable for the public status page and a longer, customer-facing postmortem that explains impact, verification steps, and optional recovery/replay choices for tenants. The goal is to be straightforward, minimize technical jargon, and give clear next steps customers can act on today.

-- Status page snippet (publish-ready) --
Summary: Brief regional degradation affecting inference responsiveness and some streaming sessions in US-West. We have applied routing mitigations; the service is in progressive recovery.
Start: 2026-10-03 14:37 UTC
Scope: ~7% of queries from US-West experienced elevated latency or truncated streaming responses for approximately 45 minutes. Affected features: streaming responses and low-traffic long-run sessions.
Current status: Recovering — most traffic normal. Ongoing verification and targeted replays available to affected tenants.
What we’re doing: Incremental capacity rebalancing and targeted traffic reroutes; automated replay tool enabled for impacted tenants.
Estimated full recovery: Completed for most customers. Operators continue verification through 2026-10-06.
Contact: support@redwood.ai (include tenant id and sample request id if available).

-- Customer-facing postmortem (concise & readable) --
TL;DR:
On 2026-10-03 we saw a regional routing/queueing regression that increased latency for a portion of US-West requests and caused some streaming sessions to truncate mid-response. We applied routing fixes and rebalanced capacity; the platform is back to normal for the majority of traffic. If you saw missing or truncated responses we provide an opt-in replay path and a short verification checklist below.

What happened (plain language):
- At 14:37 UTC a change in the request routing component caused a subset of requests to be queued longer than normal when GPU pools were briefly imbalanced. For streaming sessions this sometimes resulted in responses ending earlier than expected.
- The issue affected an estimated 7% of requests in US-West for ~45 minutes. No data exfiltration occurred and customer data was never exposed.

Immediate impact to customers:
- Some user-facing features relying on streaming may have returned shorter outputs or stopped streaming early.
- Non-streaming generation requests were largely successful but a small subset had higher latency and occasional truncation.

What we did to remediate:
1) Rerouted new traffic away from overloaded pools within 8 minutes of detection.
2) Scaled and rebalanced GPU allocation to re-establish headroom for continuous batching.
3) Enabled a targeted replay utility (tenant opt-in) that can re-run affected requests using the preserved inputs and pinned model versions.
4) Kicked off a short verification sweep across telemetry to validate output length and streaming completion rates.

How you can verify whether you were impacted (self-service steps):
1) Check your logs for request IDs between 2026-10-03 14:30–15:30 UTC originating from US-West. Look for higher-than-normal latency or truncated streaming end markers.
2) If you see truncated streams, capture one sample request id and tenant id and open a support ticket (support@redwood.ai) with subject: "Replay request: INC-8721". Include the sample id and preferred replay window.
3) Run the lightweight verification script we’ve provided in the tenant tools page (link in linked_artifacts) to confirm output length distribution pre/post-replay.

Replay and recovery options for tenants:
- Opt-in automated replay: For tenants who choose this, we will re-run queued/failed requests against the same model version and return outputs to a secure replay inbox. This is free for requests where the platform was at fault.
- Manual selective replay: Tenant operators can specify request ids to replay via the tenant console; these will be queued with priority routing.
- No-ops / accept current outputs: If your application tolerates partial outputs, no action is required.

SLA and credits:
We are evaluating SLA impact and will proactively credit tenants who experienced verified disruption beyond the normal SLO window. If you believe your SLA threshold was crossed, flag the ticket as "SLA review" and include sample evidence (request ids, timestamps).

Root cause (short):
An interaction between the routing policy update and recent autoscaling activity produced a transient state where some GPU pools were under-provisioned for the observed batching patterns. This caused queueing and premature stream terminations.

Preventative actions (what we’ll change):
- Tighten validation for routing policy changes during autoscaling events.
- Add synthetic streaming traffic tests in the US-West canary for early detection.
- Implement a short, aggressive fallback that routes streaming sessions to a warm standby pool when queue depth exceeds a low threshold.

Timeline (high-level):
- 14:37 UTC — first alerts (elevated queue depth in US-West)
- 14:45 UTC — automated detections escalate to on-call SREs
- 14:50 UTC — routing rule rollback & targeted reroutes applied
- 15:12 UTC — rebalancing and scale actions complete, progressive recovery begins
- 15:30–16:15 UTC — verification sweep and targeted replays executed for affected tenants
- 2026-10-06 — final verification and SLA assessment in progress

Customer-facing artifacts we will publish:
- Short status page update (top of this doc)
- Detailed postmortem and replay request form link (will be posted to support portal and emailed to tenants who opt in)

How we’ll notify you personally:
- If we detect that your tenant had >5% failed/truncated streaming sessions we will reach out directly with an evidence package and an invitation to opt into a complimentary replay.

Support playbook for CS reps (internal quick notes):
- Triage: ask for tenant id, 1–2 sample request ids, and approximate timestamps.
- If tenant requests replay: create a support ticket using JIRA-INC-8721 template and flag "tenant-replay-optin".
- If tenant requests SLA review: escalate to ops-licensing with evidence bundle.
- Friendly language suggestion: "We’ve rebalanced capacity and can re-run affected requests for you — if you’d like us to proceed we’ll send the outputs to a secure delivery address and walk you through verification."

Internal follow-ups (assigned owners):
- Root cause docs and long-term mitigation plan: infra/serving-runtime team (owner: Priya Menon).
- Replay mechanism improvements & audit trail: eng-platform (owner: Samir Gupta).
- Customer outreach & credits: customer-success (owner: Morgan Patel).

Open questions for the postmortem meeting:
- Should replay results be visible in the tenant console or only via secure delivery?
- What threshold triggers automatic tenant outreach (we used >5% as a starting point)?

Notes to self: polish the replay consent wording before publish; confirm legal has reviewed the wording around "no data exfiltration" claim.

--- End of doc ---
